claims.content: Customer

To browse and search auction inventory items by using one or more combinable filter/search criteria (e.g., Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Cost Range) to find matching products.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer browses and searches auction inventory items using filter/search criteria to find matching products.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Customer enters or selects one or more browse/search criteria, submits the search (e.g., via Go or Find Product), and finds the matching auction inventory product(s).
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer initiates a browse/search action by entering/selecting criteria and submitting the search.
scope_contract.success_boundary: Customer has successfully found matching product(s) through the browse/search results.
in_scope_actions: Browsing/filtering auction inventory items by product attributes and search parameters
variant_dimensions: Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location
Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Cost Range

claims.content: Auction inventory data is populated and available in the system for the Customer to browse/search.
The Customer initiates the use case by entering or selecting one or more combinable browse/search criteria and submitting the search via the 'Go' button or the 'Find Product' button.
The Customer uses the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability to browse auction inventory.

The Customer enters or selects one or more combinable browse/search criteria, such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone Type, Material Type, Material Purity, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, or Cost Range, which may be applied simultaneously.
The Customer submits the search by clicking the 'Go' button or the 'Find Product' button.

The system displays a table titled 'Search Results' containing columns for Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment, with rows showing the matching auction inventory item(s).

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of navigating via Endeca, the Customer may access the browse/search capability via a Site Map page that lists all available Categories (e.g., Jewelry, Gemstones, Collectibles, Watches), Product Types (e.g., Rings, Necklaces, Bracelets), and Gemstone Types (e.g., Tanzanite, Diamond, Ruby) as direct links to specific pages or Endeca results pages; selecting a link leads to the corresponding product results.

Diverges from Step 2: The Customer may also choose a scope for the browse/search results by selecting via radio buttons either 'Items currently online only' or 'All sellable auction inventory', and then continue with the search.

Diverges from Step 4: After the Search Results are displayed, the Customer may switch between 'List View' and 'Catalog View' display modes for the product results and continue browsing the matching products.

Diverges from Step 1: If the Customer clicks a browse/navigation link that contains no product (e.g., this routinely happens for collectibles links), the system serves a 'No Results Found' page. Exit: not specified in evidence (recovery gap listed in missing_aspects).

Diverges from Step 4: If the submitted search criteria produce no matches (e.g., a search for 'belly button'), the system displays a 'No Results Found' page that includes an apology message, a 'Search Tips' section with 5 specific suggestions to refine the search, and a 'May We Suggest' section with static and dynamically updated search terms/phrases. Exit: not specified in evidence (recovery gap listed in missing_aspects).

missing_aspects: Post-no-results recovery/continuation path is not documented in evidence for either exception branch.

claims.content: The system has applied the Customer's submitted browse/search criteria and displays a table titled 'Search Results' containing rows for the matching auction inventory product(s).

The Search Results table presents product data in the default column order: Action (checkbox), Item thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #) with link to SKU History page, Auction ID number, Description, Opening Bid, High Bid, Item Unit Cost, Start time, End time, Duration, Product Type, and Increment; Start time, End time, and Duration are initially blank for the displayed rows.

citation_audit.description: Latest model-authored candidates after internal semantic grounding verification and DRA; aligned with delivered slots.
